speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned a rash on your scalp and forehead; can you describe exactly what the skin looks like, such as whether it is red, scaly, crusted, or blistering? Have you noticed any itching, pain, or swelling in that area?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cradle Cap (Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis).

The history of a scaly rash on the scalp and forehead of a 3-month-old, which worsens in cold weather, combined with a family history of psoriasis, is highly characteristic of this condition. No further tests are required at this time.
